title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model

primary_sources.paraphrase: Abstract page, v1 of 25 Sep 2026, three authors (Atos, EDF R&D, LSCE, Orsay). French load 1 to 48 months ahead at monthly and daily resolution with a tabular foundation model; says selected economic covariates raise skill by 20% over 2015-2025, with MAPE within 4% (monthly) and 5% (daily). No code link.

Full text. National RTE load, Mar 2005 to Dec 2025; observed ERA5 weather, calendar and about 40 economic series, no load lags. Forward feature selection on 2005-2015 yields 10 subsets whose forecasts are averaged; rolling evaluation on 2016-2025, 85 forecasts per lead time. Zero-shot TabICLv2 against default XGBoost and a linear model, each with and without economic series.
SSRN posting of the same preprint by the same authors, 50 pages, 1 Oct 2026. A second copy, not peer reviewed and not an independent source.

Repository of the central model, TabICLv2. BSD 3-Clause. The default regression checkpoint is tabicl-regressor-v2-20260212.ckpt, fetched from Hugging Face; CPU inference is supported. It is the model's repository: it holds no code for the load study.
Hub record of the weights repository: licence bsd-3-clause, not gated, created 12 Feb 2026, head 4dcd344 (18 Feb 2026); contains the v2 regressor checkpoint named in the TabICL README.
Commit history of the weights repository: the checkpoints were uploaded on 12 Feb 2026 (commit d700cf0); the two later commits are README edits by their titles.

claims.text: At daily resolution, adding selected economic covariates improves TabICL by about 20% over the same model with weather and calendar inputs only, steadily across lead times of 1 to 48 months.
claims.metric: relative error reduction against the same model without economic covariates, percent (skill score on RMSE; a MAPE version is plotted too)
claims.dataset: RTE national load, France, daily; rolling forecasts 2016-2025
claims.baseline: TabICL with selected weather and calendar covariates only

claims.text: At monthly resolution the gain TabICL gets from economic covariates shrinks as the lead time grows and is close to 0% at 48 months.
claims.metric: relative error reduction against the same model without economic covariates at 48 months, percent
claims.dataset: RTE national load, France, monthly; rolling forecasts 2016-2025
claims.baseline: TabICL with selected weather and calendar covariates only

claims.text: Monthly TabICL with economic covariates stays below 4% MAPE (below 2,000 MW RMSE) at every lead time up to 48 months.
claims.dataset: RTE national load, France, monthly; rolling forecasts 2016-2025

claims.text: Monthly TabICL with economic covariates stays below 2% MAPE (below 1,000 MW RMSE) for lead times under one year.
claims.dataset: RTE national load, France, monthly; rolling forecasts 2016-2025

claims.text: Monthly XGBoost with economic covariates is at about 2.5% MAPE (about 1,400 MW) for lead times under one year, against under 2% for TabICL.
claims.dataset: RTE national load, France, monthly; rolling forecasts 2016-2025
claims.baseline: XGBoost with default hyperparameters, own selected feature subsets

claims.text: Daily forecasts with economic covariates stay below 5% MAPE (below 3,000 MW RMSE) at 48 months, for both TabICL and XGBoost.
claims.dataset: RTE national load, France, daily; rolling forecasts 2016-2025
claims.baseline: XGBoost with default hyperparameters, own selected feature subsets

claims.text: Without the feature-selection step, daily TabICL on all weather, calendar and economic covariates reaches up to 5,000 MW RMSE, against up to 3,000 MW with selection.
claims.metric: RMSE upper end over lead times, MW (no feature selection)
claims.dataset: RTE national load, France, daily; rolling forecasts 2016-2025

claims.text: Keeping only the most recent 70 to 90% of the context raises monthly TabICL's error by about 10%.
claims.metric: relative RMSE increase with reduced context, percent
claims.dataset: RTE national load, France, monthly; rolling forecasts 2016-2025

claims.text: The gain from economic covariates is not general across models: XGBoost shows almost none at monthly resolution, and the linear model none at daily resolution and only below two years at monthly resolution.
All inputs, weather and economic, are observed values for the forecast period (a hindcast) and no load lags are used; the authors say errors would be larger with forecast inputs.
The models do not agree on which economic series matter: TabICL and XGBoost pick most economic covariates in fewer than 30% of the ten feature subsets.

relevance.rationale: Electric load, but national French load at daily and monthly resolution (hourly data resampled), not an hourly zonal profile, so target_match is 2 as for other daily-load studies. The horizon is 1 to 48 months, far from our 168 hours (horizon_match 1). Temperature and other weather enter as known-future inputs using observed values, which corresponds to our oracle regime (covariates_match 3); the covariates under test, though, are economic series published monthly, quarterly or yearly, which are constant within a week and are not part of our input set.

checks.notes: pre_registered: the paper mentions no registration or frozen plan and the research call found none. The feature selection uses 2005-2015 only and the evaluation 2016-2025, but the two crisis periods analysed and the ablations were chosen with the results in hand. The abstract says 2015-2025 where the text says January 2016 to December 2025; test_window_days (3653) follows the text. evidence_strength is weak by the spec's rule: numbers without public code, and the 20% and MAPE figures are read by the authors from curves (95% bootstrap bands in figures only, hence ci90 null), with no table. A data-availability line exists but its link target was lost in the fetched text, so whether the processed dataset is public was not verified; the research call found no paper-specific GitHub, Zenodo or Hugging Face record. baseline_same_inputs: partly for the headline, because the comparison is the same model with and without economic series (same load, weather and calendar pool, feature subsets selected separately); partly against XGBoost and the linear model, which share the candidate pool but select their own subsets; XGBoost was not tuned. No naive, seasonal or time-series baseline is reported. Central model: TabICLv2. The paper names no checkpoint, package version or hardware; the weights date is taken from the Hub repository jingang/TabICL, whose name I found by a direct fetch and matched to the README's checkpoint file names, not from a statement in the paper. training_overlap_risk is about our run: checkpoints committed 12 Feb 2026, inside the scored window, with 38 of 52 scored weeks starting after it, hence med. Whether TabICL's pretraining data includes PJM or EIA-930 load was not checked. Licence BSD-3-Clause is from the repository and the Hub record. independent_replication: one research call found no replication, criticism or follow-up; the SSRN posting is the authors' own copy. discovered_via.provider is claude because the registry's first sighting is a claude scan of 13 Nov 2026; the queue row itself came from the arXiv feed, which the schema has no value for. Not checked: figures, the per-lead-time curves, appendix tables B to I, and CPU runtime of TabICL on our data. The PyPI release date of tabicl 2.2.0 comes from the research call only.

label: PARTIAL
label_reason: Relevant in subject (electric load with weather as a known-future input and a pretrained model) and sourced to its own preprint, but the evidence is thin: one unreviewed preprint with no code, a 20% gain read from curves and specific to TabICL at daily resolution, and no replication. Its headline comparison, economic series on or off at lead times of 1 to 48 months, cannot be re-measured at 168 hours with any model in runnable_models, so there is nothing to run now.
implementation_hint: Central model TabICLv2 (weights repository jingang/TabICL, file tabicl-regressor-v2-20260212.ckpt, committed 12 Feb 2026; code soda-inria/tabicl, BSD-3-Clause). It is not in runnable_models and is not a FoundationForecast wrapper, so neither models/chronos2.py nor models_ff/run_ff.py covers it; direct_adapter here means an adapter would have to be written, and CPU runtime within 60 minutes is unverified. Even with an adapter the paper's claim would not be tested: economic series do not vary within a week, and adding them would break the same-inputs rule. What could carry over is secondary only: TabICL as a tabular regressor on temperature and calendar features without load lags, as one more row against the temperature-only regression. The paper's comparators (default XGBoost, a linear model) are close to our LightGBM and regression rows.
